questions.prompt: How do you create a GET endpoint at /api/hello?

options.text: Add app/api/hello/route.ts that exports an async function named GET
Export a default function from api.ts

questions.explanation: A route.ts file with an exported GET function defines the endpoint; method-named exports handle each HTTP method.

questions.prompt: Can a single segment contain both page.tsx and route.ts?

options.text: No — a segment is either a page or a Route Handler, not both
Only if you set allowBoth in next.config.ts

questions.explanation: A segment is either UI (page.tsx) or an endpoint (route.ts). Put the API under a different path like app/api/….

questions.prompt: How do you read a JSON request body in a Route Handler? Complete: const body = await request.____();
questions.explanation: await request.json() parses the request body; it returns a promise, so you must await it.

questions.prompt: Which are good reasons to use a Route Handler? Select all that apply.

options.text: Exposing an API for a mobile app
Fetching data to render your own Server Component page
Handling a POST from an external client

questions.explanation: Route Handlers suit webhooks, external APIs, and external POSTs. For your own pages, fetch directly in a Server Component.

questions.prompt: Order the steps a POST Route Handler takes to create a resource.

items.text: Receive the Request in the exported POST function
Read the body with await request.json()

questions.explanation: A POST handler receives the request, parses the body, performs the write, and returns the created resource with a 201 status.

questions.prompt: Match each Route Handler concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: Defines an HTTP endpoint (not a page)

questions.explanation: route.ts is the endpoint file, method exports handle each verb, request.json() reads the body, and Response.json returns JSON.
